subject: a problem in transition to ggplot0.9

messages.author: 12678202871fffaa
messages.subject: a problem in transition to ggplot0.9
parts:
Dear ggplot users,
I am trying to migrate from the previous version of ggplot to the
latest version 0.9.

I have still some troubles but I am sure that the changes are
necessary in order to assure an ever greater dissemination for this
wonderful tool.

My question concerns a scatterplot with a sort of boxplot. I use the
Cars93 dataset available in the MASS package and the following two
functions to compute the crossbar limits (they essential reproduce the
box of the classical boxplot):

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(MASS)
stat_sum_single <- function(fun, geom="point", colour="red",
size=3, ...) {
stat_summary(fun.y=fun, colour=colour, geom=geom, size =
size, ...)
}
stat_sum_crossbar <- function(fun1, fun2, fun3, geom="crossbar",
colour="blue", ...) {
stat_summary(fun.y=fun1, fun.ymin=fun2, fun.ymax=fun3,
colour=colour, geom=geom, ...)
}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This plot still work properly:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggpDOT_price_origin <- qplot(data = carsRidotto, x=Origin, y=Price,
geom="point")
#confronto media vs mediana
ggpDOT_price_origin <- ggpDOT_price_origin + stat_sum_single(mean,
shape=8, size=6)
#confronto media vs 3 quartili
ggpDOT_price_origin <- ggpDOT_price_origin +
stat_sum_crossbar(function(x) quantile(x, 0.5),
function(x) quantile(x, 0.25),
function(x) quantile(x, 0.75),
geom="crossbar", colour="blue", width=0.5)
ggpDOT_price_origin
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


When I try to use the same code on a factor with three levels I have a
strange beviahour, as you can see using this code:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
carsRidotto <- subset(Cars93, Passengers %in% 4:6)
ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, Passengers, Price, geom="point")
ggp2 <- ggp + stat_sum_single(mean, shape=8, size=8)
ggp2 <- ggp2 + stat_sum_crossbar(function(x) quantile(x, 0.5),
function(x) quantile(x, 0.25),
function(x) quantile(x, 0.75),
geom="crossbar", colour="blue", width=0.5)
ggp2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


I hope that your experience could help me in solving this enigma.

Thanks in advance,
domenico

----------------------------------------------------
Domenico Vistocco
Department of Economics
University of Cassino - ITALY

> ggp2

Passengers is not a factor with three levels; it is a numeric variable
that only happens to have three distinct values. So you need to either
make it a factor:

ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, factor(Passengers), Price, geom="point")

or make Passengers a grouping aesthetic:

ggp <- qplot(data= carsRidotto, Passengers, Price, geom="point",
group=Passengers)
